sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A rare moss endemic to south-western Tasmania, formerly placed in Sphagnum. It grows on white quartz-rich alluvial sand pans and is often partly buried, so only leaf tips may be visible. Stems reach about 2 cm; stem leaves are about 3.6–4.3 mm long. A terminal capsule is raised on a pseudopodium about 3.5 mm long, rather than a typical seta.

sections.title: Uses and image note
sections.text: No food use is established. The existing plate shows the moss more exposed above the substrate than plants described in the wild; its reproductive stalk should be understood as a pseudopodium, not a long typical seta.
